Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (doubtful); Protoform: *gōḍḍ-; Proto-meaning: 'dig'

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: tákṣati; Proto-meaning: 'forms by cutting, chisels'; Analysis: Here kṣ > ch everywhere in IA area.

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Hindi; Protoform: kachuā < OIA kacchapa 'turtle, tortoise'; Proto-meaning: 'turtle, tortoise'; Analysis: Origilal Kullui form supposes a>ɔ, not a>ɛ. Palatal affricate supposes a relatively new borrowing.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (doubtful); Protoform: *pinahati; Proto-meaning: 'ties on, covers'; Analysis: Temple as a cover for brain?

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: *ḍhabba-; Proto-meaning: 'lump'; Analysis: Compensatory lenghtening of the vowel indicates a borrowing in NIA period.

Origin: It is possible to hypothesize a connection with; Source: (supposed) OIA; Protoform: caṭatkāra; Proto-meaning: 'crackling'; Analysis: Unmotivated aspiration and loss of ṭ. OIA a > NIA ɛ indicates non-Kullui historical phonetics. The phonetics is obviously corrupt.

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: akṣavāṭa-; Proto-meaning: 'wrestling ground'; Analysis: Inserted j is irregular. In original Kullui word, kṣ>tʃʰ is suggested.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *vunāti; Proto-meaning: 'weaves'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *chilla²; Proto-meaning: 'skin, rind'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: *jhamp-; Proto-meaning: 'sudden movement'; Analysis: Cf.  Skr. jhampa 'a spring, a jump',
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: sáktu; Proto-meaning: 'coarsely ground meal'; Analysis: Retention of the last vowel indicates a -ka extention in MIA.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: bhrātaraḥ; Proto-meaning: 'brothers'; Analysis: Hendriksen 154: +bra:ra m. pi. ‘brothers’. Sk. nom. pi. bhratarah + Him. pi. ending -a.
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: dzeʈʰ + ama; Proto-meaning: 'husband's elder brother' + 'mother'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: vyāghrá; Proto-meaning: 'tiger'; Analysis: Metathesis of r in MIA.

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Hindi; Protoform: pãjābi; Proto-meaning: 'Punjabi'; Analysis: From Persian panjāb '(the five waters or rivers, viz. Sutlej, Rāvi, Chināb, Jīlam, and Attock or Indus) Name of a country north-west of Hindūstān'. Palatal affricate supposes a relatively new borrowing.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Sanskrit; Protoform: trikoṇa; Proto-meaning: triangle
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (doubtful); Protoform: śr̥tá; Proto-meaning: 'boiled'; Analysis: Cerebralization is irregular.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: bhaktá; Proto-meaning: 'meal, food'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: raṇḍa; Proto-meaning: raṇḍā -- f. ʻ one deprived of or not indulging in sexual intercourse ʼ ʻ widow ʼ
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *ghuṇṭa; Proto-meaning: 'knot, tag, button'
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Persian; Protoform: kāg̠ẖaẕ; Proto-meaning: 'paper'; Analysis: Cf. Hindi kāg̣az
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Dardic; Protoform: śāh < Old Indo-Aryan  śvāsá; Proto-meaning: 'breath, breathing'; Analysis: Sibilant to h transition has parallels in Dardic languages.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: saptá; Proto-meaning: 'seven'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *bhr̥jjita; Proto-meaning: 'fried, parched'

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Mandeali; Protoform: stassi < Old Indo-Aryan  saptāśīti; Proto-meaning: 'eighty seven'; Analysis: MIA accent shifted after the loss of the final vowel in the NIA period.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Hindi; Protoform: qaincī; Proto-meaning: 'scissors'; Analysis: From Turk.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Mandeali; Protoform: chətti < Old Indo-Aryan  ṣáṭtriṁśat; Proto-meaning: 'thirty six'
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Persian; Protoform: chābuk; Proto-meaning: Quick, swift, active; ingenious, sharp, acute; beautiful; a horse-whip
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: anuhāra; Proto-meaning: 'resemblance'
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Hindi; Protoform: ghām < Old Indo-Aryan  gharma; Proto-meaning: 'heat'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: ādarśá; Proto-meaning: mirror
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: mukɳa; Proto-meaning: 'to end'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: *lōjjha-; Proto-meaning: 'defective'

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: *ḍabbara; Proto-meaning: 'mud, pool, vessel'; Analysis: Compensatory lenghtening of the vowel indicates a borrowing in NIA period.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Mandeali; Protoform: manja  < Old Indo-Aryan  mañca; Proto-meaning: 'bed sled' [Ranganatha 123] < 'stage, platform'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *dhuppā; Proto-meaning: 'sunshine'
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: gjahra; Proto-meaning: 'eleven'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: páridadhāti; Proto-meaning: 'sets round'; Analysis: Metathesis of aspiration.

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Punjabi; Protoform: marc, marcā̃ < OIA *maricca- 'peppercorn'; Proto-meaning: 'black pepper'; Analysis: Origilal Kullui form supposes a>ɔ, not a>ɛ. Dental affricate indicates an early (medieval) borrowing.

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Mandeali; Protoform: kətti < Old Indo-Aryan  ḗkatriṁśat; Proto-meaning: 'thirty one'; Analysis: Irregular changes (like weakening sibilants to h or zero) are attested among cardinal numerals since MIA period.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: trúṭyati; Proto-meaning: 'is broken, falls asunder'
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Sanskrit; Protoform: mandir < mandira; Proto-meaning: temple

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: śā́ri; Proto-meaning: 'a partic. bird' TS., śārikā- f., sā° 'Graculus religiosa or maina'; Analysis: j insertion is obscure.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: cūˊḍa, cōḍa-; Proto-meaning: 'topknot on head'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *kālakeśa; Proto-meaning: 'black-tailed'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: ṓṣṭha; Proto-meaning: 'lip'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *cōppa-; Proto-meaning: 'oily'

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Mandeali; Protoform: ṇunjaːh < Old Indo-Aryan  ūnapañcāśat; Proto-meaning: 'forty nine'; Analysis: Irregular changes (like weakening sibilants to h or zero) are attested among cardinal numerals since MIA period.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Punjabi; Protoform: khaṇḍ < Old Indo-Aryan  khaṇḍu; Proto-meaning: 'sugar'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: kīdŕ̥śa; Proto-meaning: 'Of what kind or sort, of what nature?'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: prativēśya; Proto-meaning: 'neighbour'; Analysis: Cerebralization is irregular.

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Arabic; Protoform: taq; Proto-meaning: 'an arch; an arched building, cupola, or any kind of vaulted work; a window, balcony'; Analysis: Since Arabic borrowings mostly came through Persian, meaning and transcription are done by [Steingass 1892].
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: dyuttá / dyōta; Proto-meaning: '*shining', 'injured'  / 'light'
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Arabic; Protoform: sikka; Proto-meaning: 'A die for coining'; Analysis: Source form is given by [Steingass 1892], since it matches Indian forms the most.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Persian; Protoform: narm; Proto-meaning: 'Soft to the touch'; Analysis: Source form is given by [Steingass 1892], since it matches Indian forms the most.

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: *pituḥkula X *mātr̥kula; Proto-meaning: 'father's family'; Analysis: *piwɭu > pjawɭu because of mawɭi 'mother and daughter'.

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: vákṣas; Proto-meaning: 'breast, chest'; Analysis: The word looks like a borrowing from a language where compensatory lenghtening before shortened geminates happened in the beginning of the NIA period.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Persian; Protoform: kamar; Proto-meaning: 'waist'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *mucchā; Proto-meaning: 'mustache'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: *śanaśana-; Proto-meaning: 'rustling sound'; Analysis: Origilal Kullui form supposes a>ɔ, not a>ɛ.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *khōla; Proto-meaning: 'cavity, hollow'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *ciṭaka; Proto-meaning: 'sparrow'

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Mandeali; Protoform: ṭaːppri < Old Indo-Aryan  *tarpa; Proto-meaning: 'hut'; Analysis: Unstandard metathese of r. Mand. [Ranganatha 1981: 126] ṭaːppri hut [Hendriksen 1976: 79] ʈapre f. WKc. ‘hut, small house’. J ṭaprí f. CD *tarpa1, P. ṭappaṛ m. ‘sackcloth’, ṭapprī f. ‘hut’. Compensatory lenghtening.

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Hindi; Protoform: chāl < OIA challi- 'bark'; Proto-meaning: ' Skin; rind, peel; bark'; Analysis: Compensatory lenghtening of the vowel indicates a borrowing in NIA period. Dental affricate indicates an early (medieval) borrowing.

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: kharpara + met; Proto-meaning: 'skull' (cf. Punjabi khaprā 'a kind of snake'); Analysis: By the shape of the pattern on cobra's hood. Origilal Kullui form supposes a>ɔ, not a>ɛ. Metathesis of r in MIA.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Persian; Protoform: bī-īmān; Proto-meaning: Without religion, or faith; Analysis: Source form is given by [Steingass 1892], since it matches Indian forms the most.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *mādhuka² X madhukara; Proto-meaning: 'producing honey'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: other Himachali; Protoform: trɛheṭh < Old Indo-Aryan  trayaḥṣaṣṭi; Proto-meaning: 'sixty three'; Analysis: Form is done by Bhalesi.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Sanskrit; Protoform: rākṣasá; Proto-meaning: ‘demon’; Analysis: Through other Himachali idioms (cf. Kotgarhi rāks, Kochi raːks [Hendriksen 1976: 184]).
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: ṣaṣṭhá + ma; Proto-meaning: 'sixth'
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: muɳɖ; Proto-meaning: head
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *khuṭati; Proto-meaning: 'breaks, pierces'

column4: Chudakarana, ceremony of the first haircut of a child
column10: Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *jūṭāvalavana; Proto-meaning: 'cutting hair off'; Analysis: The protoform is not attested in Turner's dictionary
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: muṣṭí; Proto-meaning: 'fist'
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: piʈʰ + dzʰuɭa; Proto-meaning: 'back' + 'bag'
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: potru; Proto-meaning: 'son's son'

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: śōdháyati; Proto-meaning: 'purifies', 'removes anything obnoxious'; Analysis: Loss of aspiration is not regular, but very common in Himachali.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: †*challī; Proto-meaning: ʻ maize ʼ; Analysis: Retention of the final vowel because of pleonastic extention (OIA -ka > MIA -a)
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: kāˊka; Proto-meaning: 'crow'
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Sanskrit; Protoform: nirguṇa; Proto-meaning: 'worthless, bad'

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: *udrōkka; Proto-meaning: 'stopped'; Analysis: Vowel reduction indicates non-standard accent placement in MIA? Vowel change in the MIA by two-mora rule (indicates a borrowing in MIA period)?
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: vāsa; Proto-meaning: 'perfume'

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Hindi; Protoform: lālcī< OIA lālitya 'amorousness'; Proto-meaning: 'greedy'; Analysis: Preservation of dental l between vowels is irregular for Kullui. Dental affricate indicates an early (medieval) borrowing.

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Persian; Protoform: nā-rāẓ; Proto-meaning: Dissatisfied, discontented, displeased; Analysis: Source form is given by [Steingass 1892], since it matches Indian forms the most.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: māma; Proto-meaning: 'uncle'
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: saf + kɛrna; Proto-meaning: 'clean' + 'do'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: ḗkaviṁśati; Proto-meaning: 'twenty one'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: vāṭa; Proto-meaning: 'enclosure, fence'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: kaṭāha; Proto-meaning: 'boiler, saucepan with handles'
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: mleɽa; Proto-meaning: yeast, sourdough
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *jhakk-⁵; Proto-meaning: 'clump, cluster'
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Persian; Protoform: ḵẖarbūza; Proto-meaning: 'A water-melon'; Analysis: аффриката! Source form is given by [Steingass 1892], since it matches Indian forms the most.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *hillati; Proto-meaning: intr. 'moves, shakes'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: malana *malati; Proto-meaning: 'crushes, rubs'

Origin: Loanword from; Source: other Himachali; Protoform: patɭa, -ɔ < pattralá '*leaf-like, thin'; Proto-meaning: ‘thin, slender’; Analysis: Ktg. Kc. J. [Hendriksen 1976: 110].Compensatory lenghtening of the vowel indicates a borrowing in NIA period.

Origin: Loanword from; Source: other Himachali; Protoform: kṭg. dhàṭṭu < OIA*dhaṭṭa- 'old cloth, loincloth'; Proto-meaning: 'woman's headgear, kerchief'; Analysis: Cf. kc. dhaṭu m. (also dhaṭhu m. 'scarf', J. dhāṭ(h)u m. [Hendriksen 1976: 105].Compensatory lenghtening of the vowel indicates a borrowing in NIA period.
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: muɳɖi; Proto-meaning: head
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: durbala; Proto-meaning: 'weak, impotent'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: phālguná; Proto-meaning: 'relating to the asterism phálgunī', 'the month February-March'
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Sanskrit; Protoform: naraka; Proto-meaning: 'hell, the place of torment'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *chātti; Proto-meaning: 'chest, breast'; Analysis: Retention of the final vowel because of pleonastic extention (OIA -ka > MIA -a)
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: ghōlayati; Proto-meaning: 'mixes, stirs together'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: vártman; Proto-meaning: 'track of a wheel, path'
Origin: Loanword from; Source: English; Protoform: cheese; Proto-meaning: 'сыр'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (doubtful); Protoform: *vētuka- or *vēḍu; Proto-meaning: 'cane, reed' 'reed, bamboo'
Source: Unknown; Protoform: слово-источник; Proto-meaning: перевод источника; Analysis: cf. Nepali cāuri 'wrinkle'.

Origin: Loanword from; Source: other Himachali[Hendriksen 1976: 154] b'adzɪ ‘vegetables, greens; mushrooms’; Protoform: b'adzɪ < Old Indo-Aryan  bharjita; Proto-meaning: ‘vegetables, greens; mushrooms’ <  ‘fried, parched’; Analysis: Cf. [Hendriksen 1976: 154] . Compensatory lenghtening indicates non-Kullui historical phonetics.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Mandeali; Protoform: khəḍna < Old Indo-Aryan  khaḍaka; Proto-meaning: 'to stand, to stop' < '*erect', 'bolt, post'; Analysis: Cf. [Ranganatha 1981: 131].
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: āmlā, āmlikā; Proto-meaning: 'tamarind tree'; Analysis: Cf. Hindi imlī 'tamarind'.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Sanskrit; Protoform: iṣṭa; Proto-meaning: 'Wished, desired'

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: *jhaṅkh¹; Proto-meaning: 'peep'; Analysis: Compensatory lenghtening of the vowel indicates a borrowing in NIA period. Also Himachali suggests vocalization of the NT-clusters. Nasalization loss is irregular.
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: age + dʰire; Proto-meaning: 'front' + 'side'
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Persian; Protoform: gala گله; Proto-meaning: an arbour, bower, projecting roof

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: cauḍá; Proto-meaning: 'relating to tonsure', n. 'the tonsure ceremony'; Analysis: Looks like a borrowing from an indiom where retroflex ḷ do not exist. But a spontaneous dentalization in Kullui or a result of MIA gemination is also possible.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: gōrūpá; Proto-meaning: 'cow-shaped'; Analysis: The MIA accent was regularly shifted to the left in NIA period after loss of the last vowel.

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Arabic; Protoform: ḥamla; Proto-meaning: 'charge, attack, assault, onset, storm'; Analysis: Since Arabic borrowings mostly came through Persian, meaning and transcription are done by [Steingass 1892].

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: pakṣá; Proto-meaning: 'wing, feather, fin, shoulder, side'; Analysis: Unmotivatet nasalization (like in many other NIA languages). OIA kṣ > NIA kh indicates non-Kullui historical phonetics.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: rā́jñī; Proto-meaning: 'queen'

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Arabic; Protoform: bālig̠ẖ; Proto-meaning: Attaining or having attained to puberty; an adult; of mature age; Analysis: Source form is given by [Steingass 1892], since it matches Indian forms the most.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Persian; Protoform: kushtī; Proto-meaning: 'Fighting; wrestling'; Analysis: Source form is given by [Steingass 1892], since it matches Indian forms the most.
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: udʒe; Proto-meaning: atop
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: jihvāˊ; Proto-meaning: 'tongue'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: jā́mātr̥; Proto-meaning: 'daughter's husband'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: mudgá + phála; Proto-meaning: 'the bean Phaseolus mungo' + 'fruit'
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: *traṭṭ; Proto-meaning: 'crackle'
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: twar; Proto-meaning: Sunday
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: gaṇḍa; Proto-meaning: 'joint of plant'; Analysis: OIA a > NIA ɛ indicates non-Kullui historical phonetics.
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: sela + tsadru; Proto-meaning: 'goat wool blanket' + 'cover'

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: kālēyaka; Proto-meaning: 'a partic. part of the intestines'  'liver'; Analysis: The shift of the accent to the left is obscure. Possible shortening of e by two mora rule after gemination of the next consonant because of Skr. borrowing to MIA (y>yy>jj).

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: bhā́ṣatē; Proto-meaning: 'speaks, says'; Analysis: ʈʰ because of paradigmatic alignment from perfective *bʰaʈʰu < *bhāṣṭa
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: dzibʰ; Proto-meaning: tongue
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: taptá; Proto-meaning: 'heated, hot'

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: *kōdravakāṣṭha; Proto-meaning: 'Paspalum scrobiculatum straw'; Analysis: The protoform is not attested in Turner's dictionary, though its parts (kōdrava 'Paspalum scrobiculatum (a grain eaten by the poor)' and kāṣṭhá 'a piece of wood or timber, a stick') are. Preservation of -dr- may indicate a borrowing from Mandeali or Punjabi.

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (with some irregular reflexes); Protoform: bāṣpá *bhāṣpa-; Proto-meaning: 'tear, tears' MBh., 'vapour' R., bāṣpaka- m. 'steam'; Analysis: Aspiration spreaded to the left.
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Arabic; Protoform: dawāʼ, diwāʼ, duwāʼ; Proto-meaning: 'medicine, remedy'

Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (irregular reflexes are attested in many languages); Protoform: prōñchati; Proto-meaning: 'wipes off'; Analysis: Assimilation of pr- and vowel change are common. Loss of aspiration is not regular, but very common in Himachali.  Vowel change (o>u) remains unexplained.
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: lɔma; Proto-meaning: long

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Arabic; Protoform: qalam; Proto-meaning: 'A pen, reed; a penknife; a knife, poniard, sword; an engraving-tool'; Analysis: Source form is given by [Steingass 1892], since it matches Indian forms the most.

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Persian; Protoform: zamī-dār; Proto-meaning: An officer under the Mughal government of Hindūstān, who (as the term imports) had charge of the land, and whose duty was to collect the revenues of the district entrusted to his superintendence, for which he was allowed a certain percentage; Analysis: Source form is given by [Steingass 1892], since it matches Indian forms the most.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan (doubtful); Protoform: *śaṭa; Proto-meaning: 'falling, rotting'; Analysis: Also an onomatopoeia is possible.
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: śŕ̊ṅga; Proto-meaning: 'horn'
Origin: Loanword from; Source: Sanskrit; Protoform: narasiṃha X ʃing; Proto-meaning: 'man-lion, Narasimha'; Analysis: Contamination with ʃing 'horn'.

Origin: Loanword from; Source: Mandeali; Protoform: trijja < Old Indo-Aryan  tr̥tīˊya; Proto-meaning: 'third' [Ranganatha 43]; Analysis: y retention as j is a result of a spontaneous gemination in the MIA period.
Origin: Derived from; Source: Kullui; Protoform: tsadər; Proto-meaning: cover
Origin: Inherited from; Source: Old Indo-Aryan; Protoform: *ghāna; Proto-meaning: 'filling'
